title: 95 unpinned tag refs for reusable GitHub Actions across the CI estate
description: Reusable actions are referenced by mutable tags (actions/checkout@v4, setup-node@v4, upload-artifact@v4); an upstream tag move would change code executed with repository secrets present.

trace.description: checkout referenced by mutable v4 tag

evidence.description: 95 tag refs counted across 41 Domain workflows; zero SHA pins (Defi and steem: 3 workflows each, same tag style)

conditions.description: Requires upstream tag move or publisher-account compromise (uncommon precondition); first-party GitHub actions reduce likelihood.

remediation.strategy: Pin used actions to full commit SHAs (dependabot or manual one-pass); no secret rotation needed.

likelihood.reason: Upstream tag move of first-party actions is an uncommon precondition.

impact.reason: Runner code executes with secrets in env.

root_cause: Workflows reference reusable actions by mutable tag refs (actions/checkout@v4, setup-node@v4, upload-artifact@v4) instead of immutable commit SHAs.
intended_behavior: Every reusable action is pinned to a full commit SHA so upstream tag movement cannot alter trusted runner code.

execution.attacker_perspective: An attacker controlling the upstream action tag or its release.
payloads: A moved or re-tagged action reference consumed on the next workflow run.
instructions: Not reproduced: no upstream modification was attempted (doctrine: no live/third-party probing).
execution.observed_result: Configuration-level observation only: mutable refs are present and consumed at run time with repository secrets in env; no execution of modified actions was performed or implied.

title: GitHub tokens embedded in remote URLs with 664 config permissions
description: All three fleet repos carry a bearer token inside the remote URL in .git/config; the config files are mode 664, so any local process able to read the worktree (including tools run by skills or agents) can obtain full read/write access to the corresponding GitHub repositories.
root_cause: Remotes were configured as https://<token>@github.com/... during fleet bootstrap; .git/config was left at default umask 664.
intended_behavior: Credential material should be provided via a credential helper or environment, and config files should be 600.

trace.description: Token embedded in remote URL for Domain
Same pattern in Defi and steem line 7

evidence.description: url = https://[REDACTED]@github.com/roshpinacare-sys/Domain.git (token present, 93-char length measured in Z-43 without printing)
stat mode of .git/config measured 664 (group/world readable), file-level observation anchored to url line

conditions.description: Single-user sandbox limits the practical reader set, but any injected skill, script, or subprocess in the session can read the file.

execution.attacker_perspective: Any local process or agent with read access to the repo worktree.
instructions: Parse the url line and extract the token.
execution.observed_result: Token present and file world-readable (measured 664; token never printed in this audit).

remediation.strategy: Switch remotes to a credential helper (or insteadOf with env-provided token) and chmod 600 the three .git/config files. Operator-level change: remotes and credentials are tier C.

likelihood.reason: Any process in the session can read the file; no multi-user exposure observed.

impact.reason: Full write access to all three fleet repos (content; no fuel/keys).

confidence.reason: Presence and mode measured directly; token length receipt exists from Z-43.

title: Gateway pivot lane proxies any localhost port on attacker-supplied query param
description: The public gateway matches XTransformPort=* and reverse-proxies to arbitrary localhost:{port}; any externally reachable client can pivot to any loopback service that lacks its own auth, not just the allowlisted services.
root_cause: The lane was designed for service routing but implemented with an unconstrained port expression.
intended_behavior: The lane should allow only enumerated service ports (e.g., 3000, 3003).

conditions.description: Only ports actually bound on loopback are reachable; the gateway host is the public exposure point.

execution.attacker_perspective: Any external client able to reach the gateway.
instructions: Send the request with the query param set to a loopback service port.
execution.observed_result: Configuration forwards to the requested localhost port (config-level observed; no live probe performed per doctrine).

remediation.strategy: Replace the wildcard matcher with an enumerated allowlist of service ports; keep the default lane unchanged.

likelihood.reason: Directly reachable by any external client if the gateway is externally exposed.

impact.reason: Blast radius limited to unauthenticated loopback services; none observed binding secrets beyond 3000/3003 in this pass.

confidence.reason: Config read directly; behavior not live-probed (doctrine: minimum local effect).

title: Default public lane serves a dev-mode server
description: The default gateway lane proxies localhost:3000 where a next dev server runs; dev mode exposes verbose diagnostics unsuitable for a public lane.
claimed_root_cause: package.json dev script is `next dev -p 3000` and platform policy mandates dev mode.

evidence.description: dev script line; gateway default lane targets localhost:3000

blockers: Exact platform-policy fact: whether this runtime may run a production build on the public lane (platform instructions currently forbid bun run build).

validation_plan.local: Reproduce a dev-mode error page locally and record the leaked diagnostics (bounded).

title: No instruction-versus-data boundary rule for the 66-skill library (108 scripts)
description: The runtime loads 66 skill definitions (108 executable scripts under skills/**) into agent context, and runtime conventions contain no rule that skill/reference content is untrusted data and never instruction — the exact class the Cloudflare AI-AND-LLM doctrine calls out for LLM-backed targets.
root_cause: Skills library predates the adoption of an explicit injection-boundary discipline.
intended_behavior: Runtime conventions must state: skill and reference content is evidence to verify, not commands to obey; executable skill scripts are inventoried and reviewed before first run.

trace.description: no untrusted-data clause found (file-level grep anchor)

evidence.description: rg for untrusted|as data|not as instruction returned empty (file-level)

conditions.description: Documentary control gap; no exploit demonstrated in this pass.

remediation.strategy: Adopt the AI-AND-LLM core-discipline clause into runtime conventions (follow-up CR; one paragraph, no code).

likelihood.reason: Skill content is regularly loaded into agent context by design.

impact.reason: Blast radius is agent behavior bounded by existing ironclads; no direct secret/execution path demonstrated.

confidence.reason: Absence measured by grep over runtime docs; counts mechanical.

execution.attacker_perspective: Content injected into a skill's markdown or reference files would be loaded into agent context and could steer agent behavior.
payloads: A SKILL.md or reference file containing instruction-shaped text (e.g., imperative directives).
instructions: Not reproduced: no payload was planted (the audit does not modify target source; the library is treated read-only).
execution.observed_result: Control-level observation only: no boundary rule exists in runtime conventions, and skill content is loaded by design; the reach of injected text into agent behavior is bounded by existing ironclads but was not experimentally demonstrated.
